contentBlocks.text: Can Foster Parents Get SASSA Grants?
Foster parents in South Africa can apply for the Foster Child Grant, which is R1,180 per month per child. This grant is specifically for children placed in foster care through the children's court.
This guide is for foster parents or relatives caring for children placed in their care through the children's court.
The Foster Child Grant exists to support foster parents who provide care for children placed in their custody by the children's court. It helps cover the costs of raising a foster child.

checklist: Must be a registered foster parent with a valid court order
The child must be placed in your care by the children's court
The child must remain in your care while receiving the grant
Must be a South African citizen or permanent resident
restrictions: The Foster Child Grant is paid until the child turns 18 (or 21 if still studying)
Foster parents can receive other grants for themselves simultaneously

steps.title: Obtain a court order
steps.description: Get a children's court order placing the child in your foster care.

steps.title: Visit your SASSA office
steps.description: Visit your nearest SASSA office with the court order, your ID, and the child's documents.

steps.title: Complete the application
steps.description: Complete the Foster Child Grant application form at the SASSA office.

steps.title: Receive payment
steps.description: Once approved, payments begin from the date of the court order.

faqs.question: Can I get the Foster Child Grant if I am a relative caring for a child?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you are a relative and have a formal foster care court order placing the child in your care, you qualify.

faqs.question: Does the Foster Child Grant stop if the child turns 18?
faqs.answer: The grant continues until the child turns 18. If the child is still in secondary or tertiary education, the grant can continue until age 21.

faqs.question: Can I receive both the Foster Child Grant and Child Support Grant?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Foster Child Grant is for the foster child in your care. You can separately apply for the Child Support Grant for your biological children.
